summary.en: Creation-Space is an Israeli space innovation hub founded in 2023 by Roy Naor, Gal Yoffe and Alon Shikar in Mitzpe Ramon ('Space City'), backed by US fund CreationsVC. Its flagship EXPAND accelerator (developed by the CreationsVC Foundation) takes cohorts of five startups developing dual-use technologies for sustainable Moon/Mars exploration and settlement, aligned with NASA's Artemis program and supported by the Israel Space Agency, with mentorship from space and AI experts including NVIDIA. The second cohort committed up to $250K per company; the EXPAND program references grants up to $3M, with a third cohort starting January 2026.

summary.en: The Israel Innovation Authority (IIA) is the support and investment arm of the Israeli government, in charge of planning and executing the country's national innovation policy. Established in 1965 as the Office of the Chief Scientist (OCS) and renamed in 2016, it runs dozens of non-dilutive grant programs (Tnufa, Startup Fund, Technological Incubators, Innovation Labs, bilateral funds and more) for entrepreneurs and companies at all stages.

summary.en: Established in 1991, the Israel Innovation Authority's Technological Incubators Program licenses ~15 incubators across Israel that turn innovative technological concepts into companies. Startups typically receive a joint public-private investment of up to NIS 5M (~$1.5M), with the Authority funding up to 85% of early-stage project costs. The program has created over 2,500 startups. A 2025 deep-tech track raises cumulative state grants to as much as NIS 21M (~$6.25M) per company.

summary.en: Yozma was the seminal 1993 Israeli government venture capital program credited with kick-starting the country's VC industry. The government invested $100M — $20M into the Yozma Fund itself and $80M matching ten new private VC funds (each requiring a foreign VC partner), retaining a 40% equity stake with a five-year buy-out option. The funds were largely privatized; the original government program ended (the Yozma Fund became the private Yozma Group in 1997).

strategy.thesis: The first fully tokenized VC fund, investing in blockchain ecosystem-building and tokenization (RWA / digital securities) companies, providing liquidity to LPs via tradable security tokens.

summary.en: SPiCE VC is the first fully tokenized venture capital fund, founded in 2017 by Israeli entrepreneur Tal Elyashiv (co-founded with Carlos Domingo, who went on to found Securitize). It invests in blockchain ecosystem and tokenization (RWA / digital securities) companies and is operated across Singapore, the US and Israel. SPiCE I closed in 2018 (raising $15M in a 2018 STO toward a $100M target) and SPiCE II closed in 2023; the fund reports over 2.1x DPI.

summary.en: The Mamram Blockchain Incubator (M.B.I), launched in 2024 by the Mamram Alumni Association (8,000+ IDF central computing unit veterans), is Israel's first dedicated blockchain/Web3 incubation program. It supports founders from the ideation stage with mentorship and technology partnerships from StarkWare, Fireblocks and Collider VC, plus legal support from Gornitzky & Co. Investment amount, equity and cohort details are not publicly disclosed.
